edu-dopamine-01.title: Wanting is not the same as liking
edu-dopamine-01.summary: A short check after the dopamine sheet: what the messenger is actually tied to.
edu-dopamine-01.goal: Distinguish dopamine’s role in wanting and learning from the idea that it is “the pleasure molecule”.
edu-dopamine-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, dopamine is most closely tied to which of these?
edu-dopamine-01.explain: The sheet links dopamine more to wanting, learning from prediction error, and deciding what is worth trying than to pleasure itself. Liking depends on several systems. A sudden rise is not the same as being happier.

options.wanting: Wanting, learning, and deciding what is worth trying
options.pleasure: Pleasure itself — it is “the pleasure molecule”
options.meter: A personal meter of days without use

edu-serotonin-01.title: Not a happiness tank
edu-serotonin-01.summary: A check after the serotonin sheet: what 5-HT does and does not measure.
edu-serotonin-01.goal: See why calling serotonin “the happiness molecule” compresses too much, including the split between blood and brain.
edu-serotonin-01.prompt: Why is it misleading to treat serotonin as “the happiness molecule”?
edu-serotonin-01.explain: 5-HT modulates many systems at once. A sudden rise is not more happiness. Most of the body’s serotonin is not in the brain, and the molecule does not freely cross the blood–brain barrier, so a change in blood serotonin is not a reading of brain serotonin.

options.many_systems: It modulates many systems; a rise is not more happiness, and blood serotonin is not brain serotonin
options.blood_equals_brain: A blood test is a direct reading of brain serotonin and mood
options.happiness_tank: Serotonin exists only in the brain, where it fills a happiness tank

edu-gaba-01.title: Inhibition is not switching the brain off
edu-gaba-01.summary: A check after the GABA sheet: what “inhibitory” means in a network.
edu-gaba-01.goal: Understand GABA as a way some neurons fire less or with a different rhythm — not as a universal off switch or as alcohol itself.
edu-gaba-01.prompt: What does it mean that GABA is the main inhibitory messenger in the adult brain?
edu-gaba-01.explain: To inhibit is to make some neurons less likely to fire, or to fire with a different rhythm. It is not “switching the brain off.” Alcohol is not GABA: among other actions, it can potentiate some GABA-A receptors so they answer more strongly to GABA already there.

options.network_brake: It makes some neurons less likely to fire, or changes their rhythm — it does not switch the brain off
options.brain_off: It switches the whole brain off, which is the same as sleep
options.alcohol_is_gaba: Alcohol is GABA, so a drink replaces the messenger

edu-receptors-01.title: Occupying a receptor is not the same as activating it
edu-receptors-01.summary: A check after the receptors sheet: agonists, antagonists, and cocaine’s contrast.
edu-receptors-01.goal: Separate activation from occupancy, and receptor action from blocking a transporter.
edu-receptors-01.prompt: On the educational sheet, how do an agonist and an antagonist differ?
edu-receptors-01.explain: An agonist activates the receptor, or a substantial fraction of its activity. An antagonist occupies the site without mimicking that activation. Cocaine’s best-known dopaminergic move is not opening a dopamine receptor: it blocks DAT, so dopamine already released is cleared more slowly.

options.occupancy: An agonist activates (or a large fraction of that activity); an antagonist occupies without mimicking that activation
options.same_name: They are two names for the same ligand at the same door
options.cocaine_is_key: Cocaine is a key that opens D1 and D2 receptors the way nicotine opens nicotinic ones

edu-tolerance-01.title: Tolerance is not addiction
edu-tolerance-01.summary: A check after the tolerance sheet: a change of sensitivity, not a diagnosis.
edu-tolerance-01.goal: Define pharmacological tolerance without equating it with addiction or with a tank running dry.
edu-tolerance-01.prompt: What does pharmacological tolerance mean in this educational sheet?
edu-tolerance-01.explain: Tolerance is a drop in the response to the same dose when exposure is repeated. It is not a moral judgement and not, by itself, addiction or a substance use disorder. It is not the brain simply running out of a messenger, and Soma cannot assign you a universal curve.

options.sensitivity: A drop in response to the same dose with repeated exposure — not the same as addiction
options.equals_addiction: Proof of addiction; one weaker coffee is enough to diagnose a disorder
options.empty_tank: The brain running out of the messenger, on a curve Soma can read in you

edu-neuroadaptation-01.title: Adaptation is not the same as damage
edu-neuroadaptation-01.summary: A check after the neuroadaptation sheet: plasticity versus loss of cells.
edu-neuroadaptation-01.goal: Distinguish functional change in circuits from neurodegeneration, and from a fixed recovery calendar.
edu-neuroadaptation-01.prompt: How does the sheet distinguish neuroadaptation from neurodegeneration?
edu-neuroadaptation-01.explain: Neuroadaptation is mainly a change of function — plasticity — and sometimes of synapse architecture. Neurodegeneration is loss or injury of nerve cells. They are not the same thing, and stopping use does not reset the nervous system on a universal calendar this app can apply.

options.plasticity: Neuroadaptation is mainly functional change; neurodegeneration is loss or injury of nerve cells
options.cell_death: Every adaptation to caffeine or nicotine is the same as losing neurons
options.fixed_calendar: They are the same process, and the brain returns to a snapshot on a fixed number of days
